react_result.final_narrative_text: Three orthogonal pathway-enrichment paradigms converged on Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism as the dominant affected pathway in the treatment group. RaMP multi-database ORA (FDR 1.30×10⁻⁸, fold-enrichment 758) ranked KEGG:map00260 first; Mummichog m/z-direct activity against the human metabolic-function network (p=0.0078) independently ranked the same pathway first; and MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA (p=0.004) confirmed it as the top hit (hsa00260). Four driver metabolites were verified across all three tool result sets: L-threonine (KEGG:C00188), choline (KEGG:C00114), L-glutamic acid (KEGG:C00025), and dihydrolipoic acid (KEGG:C02147). L-Threonine feeds into the pathway as a direct precursor to glycine via L-serine, and its differential abundance implicates amino-acid catabolism and one-carbon metabolism. Choline enters as a methyl-group donor whose oxidation product, betaine, interfaces with serine hydroxymethyltransferase flux. L-Glutamic acid is the transamination partner at the serine–glycine node and also links to nicotinamide metabolism (NAD⁺ biosynthesis), providing a secondary mechanistic bridge. The secondary consensus hit, nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism (KEGG:map00760), appeared in RaMP (FDR 6.97×10⁻⁴) and Mummichog (p=0.018) and shares L-glutamic acid as the overlapping driver, reinforcing a perturbation of the glutamate–NAD⁺ axis. Together, the data suggest that the treatment drives amino-acid catabolism, one-carbon folate cycling, and NAD⁺ salvage, with dihydrolipoic acid pointing to secondary mitochondrial energy-chain involvement.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three orthogonal pathway-enrichment paradigms converged on Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism as the dominant affected pathway in the treatment group. RaMP multi-database ORA (FDR 1.30×10⁻⁸, fold-enrichment 758) ranked KEGG:map00260 first; Mummichog m/z-direct activity against the human metabolic-function network (p=0.0078) independently ranked the same pathway first; and MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA (p=0.004) confirmed it as the top hit (hsa00260). Four driver metabolites were verified across all three tool result sets: L-threonine (KEGG:C00188), choline (KEGG:C00114), L-glutamic acid (KEGG:C00025), and dihydrolipoic acid (KEGG:C02147). L-Threonine feeds into the pathway as a direct precursor to glycine via L-serine, and its differential abundance implicates amino-acid catabolism and one-carbon metabolism. Choline enters as a methyl-group donor whose oxidation product, betaine, interfaces with serine hydroxymethyltransferase flux. L-Glutamic acid is the transamination partner at the serine–glycine node and also links to nicotinamide metabolism (NAD⁺ biosynthesis), providing a secondary mechanistic bridge. The secondary consensus hit, nicotinate and nicotinamide metabolism (KEGG:map00760), appeared in RaMP (FDR 6.97×10⁻⁴) and Mummichog (p=0.018) and shares L-glutamic acid as the overlapping driver, reinforcing a perturbation of the glutamate–NAD⁺ axis. Together, the data suggest that the treatment drives amino-acid catabolism, one-carbon folate cycling, and NAD⁺ salvage, with dihydrolipoic acid pointing to secondary mitochondrial energy-chain involvement.
